```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  prompt = FALSE
)
library(readjsa)

fixture <- function(name) {
  installed <- system.file("extdata", name, package = "readjsa")
  candidates <- c(
    installed,
    file.path("..", "inst", "extdata", name),
    file.path("inst", "extdata", name)
  )
  path <- candidates[nzchar(candidates) & file.exists(candidates)]
  if (!length(path)) stop("The packaged fixture is missing: ", name)
  path[[1L]]
}

capture_error <- function(expr) {
  tryCatch(
    force(expr),
    error = function(error) {
      data.frame(
        class = class(error)[[1L]],
        message = conditionMessage(error),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    }
  )
}
```

`readjsa` fails closed when a source cannot be identified or no longer matches
the supported schema. This is preferable to returning plausible-looking data
with the wrong family, geography, vintage, or unit. The examples below use
only the packaged fixtures, so they are safe to run without network access.

## Check the file and family first

The local readers validate the extension before opening a file. A CSV passed to
the IVI reader is a `readjsa_file_error`; it is not interpreted as a workbook.

```{r wrong-extension}
capture_error(
  read_ivi_file(fixture("salm_sa2.csv"), family = "skill_states")
)
```

A file can also be valid in general but incompatible with the selected family.
For example, an SA2 CSV is not an LGA release: its preamble and identifier
headers state a different geography and ASGS context.

```{r wrong-geography}
capture_error(
  read_salm_file(fixture("salm_sa2.csv"), geography = "lga")
)
```

Use `jsa_release_manifest()` to inspect supported family IDs, and pass the
family/geography that matches the file. Do not infer an IVI family from a
filename if the workbook's sheet layout is available.

## Understand publication statuses

An unavailable or not-published token is not an ordinary numeric zero. SALM
retains the token in `raw_value`, sets `value` to `NA`, and records the reason
in `observation_status`.

```{r statuses}
salm <- read_salm_file(fixture("salm_sa2.csv"), geography = "sa2")
salm[salm$observation_status != "published", c(
  "date", "geography_code", "data_item", "value",
  "observation_status", "raw_value"
)]
```

REOS percentage values are canonical decimal proportions. IVI and SALM values
retain their declared units in `unit` and `unit_multiplier`. Always use those
fields when combining families or presenting a chart.

## Diagnose discovery failures offline

Discovery errors commonly mean that a publication page has gained an
unclassified link, has lost one of the expected current families, or no longer
contains a parseable reference period. With a local page, the same validation
can be inspected without a network call:

```{r discovery-error}
capture_error(
  discover_jsa_releases("ivi", html = fixture("reos.html"))
)
```

The error class `readjsa_discovery_error` identifies a catalogue problem. On a
live page, check the publisher's page manually and preserve the exact URL and
release date before retrying. `strict = TRUE` (the default) refuses partial or
ambiguous catalogues; it should not be disabled merely to make a pipeline
continue with an unknown family.

## Network and cache failures

The network-enabled readers require approved initial and final HTTPS URLs,
apply timeouts, retries, and received-file-size checks, and use a user cache.
They do not require a credential. A `readjsa_transport_error` usually indicates
an HTTP or transport failure; a `readjsa_size_error` indicates a configured
size bound; and a
`readjsa_cache_error` indicates a lock, metadata, or final verification
failure. For an offline run, use the local `*_file()` readers and a saved raw
file instead of repeatedly retrying a network call.

The cache can be inspected with `jsa_cache_dir()`. It is safe to remove an
invalid cache entry and fetch the saved catalogue row again, but keep the raw
file and complete `raw_sha256` when an audit trail matters. The
[reproducibility and cache](reproducibility-and-cache.html) article shows a
temporary offline cache replay.

## Provenance and changed releases

`readjsa_provenance_error` means that release metadata conflicts with the exact
file: for example, the latest observation date does not match the declared
reference period, or a supplied hash does not match the bytes. Treat this as a
real data-integrity signal. Do not overwrite provenance columns to silence it;
re-check that the source file, catalogue row, and family selection belong
together.

Finally, report the package version, dataset/family, source filename, reference
period, and complete `raw_sha256` when emailing a report to chartwellmacro@gmail.com. That information lets
another user distinguish a changed publisher release from a local file or
environment problem.
